description:
SECTION: Documentation as contract

CONTRACT RISK
Two HashMap<String, _> fields on Message do not document what the
String key represents:

  src/message.rs  Message.reactions: HashMap<String, Reaction>
                  /// The `reactions` property (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §4.11).

  src/message.rs  Message.delivery_receipts: Option<HashMap<String, DeliveryReceipt>>
                  /// The `deliveryReceipts` property (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §4.11).

For both, the doc comment cites the spec section but does NOT tell a
caller what the key is. Looking at the test fixtures:

  reactions:         "r1" => Reaction { emoji, senderId, sentAt, ... }
  delivery_receipts: "u1" => DeliveryReceipt { deliveredAt, readAt, ... }

The keys appear to be a reaction id and a recipient ChatContact id
respectively, but neither the spec citation nor the field doc
makes that explicit.

WHAT BREAKS FOR CALLERS
- A caller writing `for (key, reaction) in &msg.reactions` cannot
  tell whether `key` is the reaction id (for lookup operations), the
  emoji (for grouping), the sender id (for who-reacted lookup), or
  something else. They guess wrong and either pass the wrong value
  into another JMAP method or silently miss data.
- For delivery_receipts, a caller writing per-recipient UI cannot
  tell whether the key is a SenderId-shape value ("self" or
  ChatContact.id), or a raw ChatContact.id, or an Account id, or
  something else. The semantics around the "self" sentinel
  (JMAP-ly0n.1) compound this — the key's relationship to SenderId
  matters but is not documented.
- Iterating in a stable order is not possible; the doc does not
  state whether iteration order matters per spec. (HashMap iteration
  order is intentionally random in Rust.)

WHY THIS IS API-CONTRACT, NOT JUST A DOC NIT
The fields are `pub` HashMap with a public key type of String. The
key semantics are part of the API contract whether the maintainer
wants them to be or not. Callers will eventually pin behaviour to
their guess at what the key means; once they ship, the maintainer
cannot retroactively change the contract without breaking them.

RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION
Add a single doc sentence to each field naming the key shape, with
a spec citation. Example shape (matching what the test fixtures imply):

  /// The `reactions` property (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §4.11).
  ///
  /// Map key: the server-assigned reaction id (an [`Id`] string in
  /// JMAP terms; kept as `String` so the JSON object's natural key
  /// shape is preserved). Iteration order is not specified.

  /// The `deliveryReceipts` property (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §4.11).
  ///
  /// Map key: the recipient's `ChatContact.id` (per the spec, the
  /// account owner's own receipt — if present — is keyed by the
  /// "self" sentinel; see [`SenderId`] for the latitude on that
  /// sentinel).

Optionally, change the key type to `Id` where the spec says the
key is an id — but the wire format requires String keys in JSON
objects, so the doc is the more sustainable fix.

ORACLE
draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §4.11 (Message); existing field-doc style
elsewhere in the same struct (every other field carries a spec
citation).
title: HashMap<String, _> fields do not document what the key represents (Message.reactions, Message.delivery_receipts)
